results.title: the platform audit log on the Management API
results.detail: 115 paths in the /v1 spec; 0 mention audit - the platform audit log has no read path, no export path and no delete path on the public API. It is Dashboard-only, which is why no tenant credential can rewrite it and also why nobody can pull it into a SIEM.

results.title: logged statements in the last hour, by role and application_name
results.detail: postgres/mgmt-api x14, postgres/supabase/dashboard-query-editor x1. Every path this harness uses arrives as one role, so a per-person question cannot be answered from Postgres alone.

results.title: a Dashboard SQL Editor session, if the operator step has been run
results.detail: found the operator statement: role=postgres, application_name=supabase/dashboard-query-editor. That is the identity a Dashboard member's SQL runs as.

results.title: audit-log keys in the documented auth config
results.detail: GET config/auth -> HTTP 200, 243 keys returned, 1 of them mention audit (audit_log_disable_postgres=true). audit_log_disable_postgres is present and reads true.

results.title: PATCH audit_log_disable_postgres through the Management API
results.detail: asked for audit_log_disable_postgres=false (the opposite of the true it held). PATCH -> HTTP 200; on re-read the key is true. A 2xx that leaves the value unchanged: the switch is accepted and ignored on the public API, so it is Dashboard-only (Authentication -> Configuration -> Audit Logs).

results.title: does a new auth event still reach the table
results.detail: admin user create -> HTTP 200 in 1 attempt(s); password login -> HTTP 200. Table rows 0 -> 0; a row tagged with this run did not appear within 121s. On a fresh project the Postgres copy is OFF by default.

results.title: cleanup
results.detail: auth config PATCH reverted; test user deleted

results.title: install a chained mirror fed by a trigger on the audit table
results.detail: schema, chained table, SECURITY DEFINER capture function, verifier and trigger created; 1 trigger now on auth.audit_log_entries. A tenant CAN attach a trigger to the Auth server's own table - the ACL grants postgres the TRIGGER privilege.

results.title: a real auth event reaches the mirror through the trigger
results.detail: admin user create -> HTTP 200, password login -> HTTP 200; the mirror captured nothing within 125s. Mirror holds 0 rows (seq null..null); verifier: 0 rows checked, first break none. GoTrue writes as supabase_auth_admin and the SECURITY DEFINER function still records it.

results.title: delete one mirror row: does the verifier notice
results.detail: could not delete a mirror row: no second row to delete

results.title: the same identity rebuilds the chain and the verifier goes quiet
results.detail: rehash of every row -> true; verifier now reports first break none over 0 rows. The head hash moved from ... to ..., so the ONE thing that survives an owner with a rehash loop is a head hash that was copied out of the database before the tampering. In-database immutability against the database owner does not exist; off-box anchoring is the control.

results.title: cleanup
results.detail: trigger and schema dropped (0 user triggers left on the audit table); test user deleted
